title: lane run survives an outside repository and concurrent lanes end to end
body:
Why: the first outside pilot (krn-works/seo-audit-harness, t-djnrw3t) found six lane-run defects one expensive session at a time (fixed in f06353c 21f77d4 c6f0efd 062a4a9 23d23ea); three more remain: (1) parallel `krn lane start` races on `git fetch origin main` ("cannot lock ref refs/remotes/origin/main", exit 64; .krn/runs/pilot/lanes/summary.txt); (2) parallel lanes run their red-baseline check at once and the pilot suite times out under load, so every lane refuses with exit 72 although the suite is green alone (.krn/runs/pilot/lanes/baseline-solo.log: 271 files pass); (3) the exit-72 detail quotes vitest's separator line instead of the failing test names. Root cause of all nine: lane-run tests use fakes of the receiver, never an outside-shaped repository (KRN-12).
Outcome: concurrent lane starts in one repository succeed (fetch serialized or retried on a ref lock); baseline checks of concurrent lanes are serialized by a lock under the main checkout's .krn/; a red baseline names the failing test files; a preflight before the model session fails in seconds on a missing settings file, unusable token or unreachable remote; and an end-to-end test runs `krn lane run` on a generated outside-shaped repository (no root package.json, code in packages/x, krn.json contract with --prefix, local bare remote) with a scripted session (KRN_LANE_CLAUDE) that writes the commit the way Claude does (Ticket line, blank line, Co-Authored-By) and reaches the ship step.
Proof: the e2e test fails on main before the fixes for at least the sandbox-placeholder and fetch-race cases and passes after; npm run fast PASS.

Scope addition (lead): pilot lanes run one at a time still refuse with exit 72 (summary.txt, last 4 rows) while the same baseline passes by hand (baseline-solo.log); the pilot suite is timing-flaky under host load. When the baseline is red, rerun only the failing test files once; refuse with exit 72 only when they fail again, and name them in the detail. Test this at the lowest layer.
